… [?], yet the success in obtaining men of talent through selection across the dynasties, as well as their methods of instruction, can also [be known / be examined?]. After the methods of selection and military training of the flourishing Zhou dynasty fell into disuse, the Han dynasty instituted selections from among sons of respectable families (liangjiazi), archers of the Six Commandries, recruited cavalrymen, and those who achieved military merit. For instance, Li Guang (李廣) achieved merit in every battle and repeatedly repelled the Chanyu; Zhao Chongguo (趙充國) submitted illustrated strategic plans and effortlessly hemmed in the Western Qiang; and others such as Gongsun He (公孫賀), Fu Jiezi (傅介子), and Gan Yanshou (甘延壽) were all renowned generals of the time who generally achieved military merit. From this, one can know how the military examinations of the Han succeeded in obtaining men of talent. The military examinations of the Tang dynasty tested candidates in long-range archery (changduo), mounted archery, foot archery, mounted lance, lifting the city-gate bolt (qiaoguan), weight-carrying, and physique. During the Tianbao era (742–756), a category for mastery of the military methods of Sunzi and Wuzi (Sun Wu bingfa) was added, from which Pei Duanfu (裴端復) and Guo Ziyi (郭子儀) both emerged. While Pei's achievements were not prominent, Ziyi restored the Tang imperial house and his merit overshadowed the entire realm; thus, one can see how the military examinations of the Tang succeeded in obtaining men of talent. During the Kaibao era (968–976) of the Song dynasty, there was the recruitment of those "versed in civil administration as the warp and military strategy as the weft" (wenjing wuwei), and during the Tiansheng era (1023–1032), following the Tang system, the category of military strategy and martial arts (junmou wuyi) was established, from which Gao Zhining (高志寧) and Linghu Ting (令狐挺) both emerged. Zhining predicted that Yuanhao (元昊) would certainly rebel, and his words proved true, so that Han Qi (韓琦) compared his ability to gauge the enemy to that of the Marquis of Huaiyin [Han Xin 韓信]; Ting advised Di Qing (狄青) to strike at the unguarded points of Nong Zhigao (儂智高), and Bi Zhongyou (畢仲游) said of him that he could strategize across ten thousand li. In the Song military examinations, these two men were the foremost. Others included Ma Long (馬隆) [?], who achieved victory with arrayed carts [reading 編廂 as 偏箱], and Han Shizhong (韓世忠), who routed the Jurchens (Jin) with his troops; such was the success of the Song military examinations in obtaining men of talent.

As for the establishment of the Military School (Wuxue), its name began when Emperor Dezong of the Tang converted the Temple of Taigong (Taigong miao) into a Military School. Emperor Shenzong of the Song [note: chronologically after Renzong's Qingli era, though the text places Shenzong first] established a Military School at the Temple of Martial Completion (Wucheng miao), appointing Han Zhen (韓縝), Director of a Bureau in the Ministry of War, to administer school affairs (pan xueshi). He instructed the sons and younger brothers of generals and officials in military methods and the ways in which troops were employed through the ages; all those who qualified in three examinations were appointed as military officers, though it was later abolished due to critics' objections. title: 正統七年會試錄
text:
聖朝文運大興治教昭明設科以取士執事典文衡策多
士以古之師道為問甚盛心也敢不摭所聞以對夫
師者明聖人之道以為教師得其人則教道立賢才
多論者謂為師者莫過於宋之胡安定也其次則孫
明復石守道焉安定之在湖學也置經義治事二齋
學者居之以講論討習如治兵治民治水之類而謂
其教有體用者何哉君臣父子仁義禮樂歷世不可
變者體也詩書子傳垂於後世者文也舉而施之天
下國家能潤澤生民者用也當時從安定游者若錢
===
藻之淵篤孫覺之純明范純仁之直溫與劉彝錢公
輔諸人者皆為名臣非有得於體用之教歟及入判
國子學者常數千人其所以為教不外於體用之學
也或謂其教乃科舉之學此豈知安定者乎程伊川
之明道學徐仲積之有孝行嘗游其門非大儒歟非
有節操之君子歟其學果進取之業歟明復居泰山
之陽著尊王發微一書其學邃其行純為魯名儒人
稱為泰山先生守道則貧而力學行誼甚高嘗仕于
朝慶曆之頌至今人猶傳誦故當時之士以徂徠為魯

punctuated: 聖朝文運大興，治教昭明，設科以取士。執事典文衡，策多士，以古之師道為問，甚盛心也，敢不摭所聞以對？夫師者，明聖人之道以為教。師得其人，則教道立、賢才多。論者謂為師者莫過於宋之胡安定也，其次則孫明復、石守道焉。安定之在湖學也，置「經義」、「治事」二齋，學者居之以講論討習，如治兵、治民、治水之類。而謂其教有體用者，何哉？君臣、父子、仁義、禮樂，歷世不可變者，體也；《詩》、《書》、子、傳，垂於後世者，文也；舉而施之天下國家，能潤澤生民者，用也。當時從安定游者，若錢藻之淵篤、孫覺之純明、范純仁之直溫，與劉彝、錢公輔諸人者，皆為名臣，非有得於體用之教歟？及入判國子，學者常數千人，其所以為教，不外於體用之學也。或謂其教乃科舉之學，此豈知安定者乎？程伊川之明道學、徐仲積之有孝行，嘗游其門，非大儒歟？非有節操之君子歟？其學果進取之業歟？明復居泰山之陽，著《尊王發微》一書，其學邃，其行純，為魯名儒，人稱為「泰山先生」。守道則貧而力學，行誼甚高，嘗仕于朝，慶曆之頌至今人猶傳誦。故當時之士以徂徠為魯…
translation_en:
…our Sacred Dynasty, literary fortune flourishes greatly, governance and education are bright and clear, and examination categories have been established to select scholars. You, Sir, hold the balance of literary assessment and pose policy questions to the multitude of scholars, asking about the Way of the teacher in antiquity. This is a mostmagnanimous intention! How could I dare not gather what I have heard in order to reply?

Now, a teacher is one who clarifies the Way of the sages so as to provide instruction. When the right person is found to be a teacher, the Way of instruction is established and worthy talents become numerous. Commentators say that among those who served as teachers, none surpassed Hu Anding 胡安定 (Hu Yuan 胡瑗) of the Song, followed next by Sun Mingfu 孫明復 (Sun Fu 孫復) and Shi Shoudao 石守道 (Shi Jie 石介). When Anding was at the Huzhou 湖州 prefectural school, he established two halls, "Classical Meaning" (Jingyi 經義) and "Practical Administration" (Zhishi 治事), where students resided to lecture, discuss, investigate, and practice subjects such as military administration, civil governance, hydraulic management, and the like. Why is it said that his teaching possessed both substance (ti 體) and function (yong 用)? Sovereign and minister, father and son, benevolence and righteousness, ritual and music—those things that cannot be changed across the generations—are its substance; the Odes (Shi 詩), the Documents (Shu 書), the Masters (zi 子), and the commentaries (zhuan 傳)—those things handed down to later generations—are its literary expression (wen 文); raising these up and applying them to the empire and the state so as to enrich and benefit the living people is its function. At that time, those who studied under Anding—such as Qian Zao 錢藻 with his deep earnestness, Sun Jue 孫覺 with his pure clarity, Fan Chunren 范純仁 with his upright warmth, along with men like Liu Yi 劉彝 and Qian Gongfu 錢公輔—all became renowned ministers. Was this not because they gained something from his teaching of substance and function? When he entered the capital to serve as Administrator of the Directorate of Education (pan Guuzi 判國子), his students regularly numbered several thousand, and the means by which he taught did not go beyond the learning of substance and function. Some claim that his teaching was merely learning for the civil service examinations—how could such people truly understand Anding? Cheng Yichuan 程伊川 (Cheng Yi 程頤), who illuminated the Learning of the Way (Daoxue 道學), and Xu Zhongji 徐仲積 (Xu Ji 徐積), who was noted for his filial conduct, once studied at his gate. Were they not great Confucians? Were they not gentlemen of moral integrity? Was their learning really just a pursuit for career advancement?

Mingfu lived on the southern slope of Mount Tai 泰山 and authored the book Expositions on Revering the King (Zunwang fawei 尊王發微). His learning was profound and his conduct pure; he was a renowned Confucian of Lu 魯, and people called him the "Master of Mount Tai" (Taishan xiansheng 泰山先生). Shoudao, for his part, was poor yet studied diligently, and his conduct and righteousness were весьма lofty. He once served at court, and his "Eulogy of the Qingli Reign" (Qingli zhi song 慶曆之頌) is still recited and passed down by people to this day. Therefore, the scholars of that time regarded Mount Culai 徂徠 as the pride of Lu…

之望守道魯人所尊稱為徂徠先生二人之學行與
安定並稱者盖有所自也為師者舎是其誰歟愚
也未能悉知惟執事進而教之幸甚

translation_en: … the model of [Lu]. Shoudao (Shi Jie 石介) was revered by the people of Lu, who called him Master Culai (Culai xiansheng 徂徠先生). That the learning and conduct of these two men (Sun Fu 孫復 and Shi Jie) were spoken of alongside those of Anding (Hu Yuan 胡瑗) indeed had its basis. As for those who serve as teachers, if one sets these men aside, who else is there? In my ignorance I have not been able to comprehend this fully; I would be most fortunate if Your Excellency would admit me and instruct me.

會試錄後序

文章之作，豈無所本哉？德之有諸中者，發於言而成章之謂文；達之天下，以明君臣、父子、夫婦、長幼、朋友之理，則所謂貫道之器也。用是黼黻皇猷，用是敷宣治化，著之為書，炳炳琅琅，垂之千萬世而不可泯者，若昔臯陶之賡歌，周、召之告戒，用康兆民者是已。後世大賢君子，發於言論，措諸事為，盡忠君愛民之誠，卓然弼成一代之治者，亦豈非其中之有所本者歟？其間由科目而進，文行政事為後世稱羨者，亦未嘗無也。我
translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Metropolitan Examination

How could the composition of literary writings be without a foundation? When virtue is possessed within, its expression in words so as to form an accomplished pattern is called literature; when extended throughout the realm to elucidate the principles governing ruler and minister, father and son, husband and wife, elder and younger, and friends, it is what is called a vessel that carries the Way. By this means one adorns the imperial counsels; by this means one proclaims the transforming influence of governance. Written down in books, brilliant and resonant, handed down for ten thousand generations without ever perishing—such were the antiphonal songs of Gao Yao in antiquity and the admonitions of the Dukes of Zhou and Shao, through which they brought peace to the myriad people. In later ages, great worthies and noble men expressed this in their discourses and applied it in their deeds, exhausting their sincerity in loyalty to the ruler and love for the people, and eminently assisting in bringing about the good governance of an entire era—how could this, too, not be because they possessed a foundation within? 誠用裨益治道言必德言行必實
punctuated: 朝文運弘開，列聖相承，治臻隆平，最重於進士之選。乃正統壬戌春二月，會試天下貢士，閱其文浩然沛然，舂容可取者甚多。盖諸士子蒙國家教養之恩，樂菁莪、豈弟之化，涵濡既久，又遭際聖天子在位，重熙累洽之日，挾其藝而來，得盡發其胸中之所蘊，故以其文登名於是選也，豈不宜哉？行將對揚大廷，駸駸然躋于顯融矣。尤當以遠大自期，蚤夜思所以報稱，竭其忠誠，用裨益治道。言必德言，行必實
translation_en:
… Dynasty, literary fortune has opened up broadly. As successive Sacred Emperors inherited the throne from one another and governance reached flourishing peace, they placed the greatest importance on the selection of metropolitan graduates (jinshi). Now, in the second month of spring of the renxu year of the Zhengtong era (1442), the tribute scholars (gongshi) of the realm were tested at the Metropolitan Examination. Upon reviewing their essays, there were very many that were vast and abundant, composed with calm leisure and worthy of selection. Indeed, these scholars have received the grace of the state's education and nurture, rejoicing in the transformative influence of "Luxuriant Tarragon" (Jing'e) and "Easy and Amiable" (Kaidi) [from the Book of Odes]. Having been steeped and nourished in this for so long, and further encountering a time of cumulative splendour and harmony with the Sacred Son of Heaven on the throne, they have come bearing their literary skills and have been able to fully express what is stored within their breasts. Therefore, is it not fitting that through their writings their names are entered into this selection?

Soon they will respond to the Emperor's questions in the Great Court [at the Palace Examination] and swiftly ascend to prominence and distinction. All the more should they set lofty and far-reaching expectations for themselves, pondering day and night how to repay their sovereign and match their station, exhausting their loyalty and sincerity so as to benefit the way of governance. Their words must be words of virtue, their deeds must be substantive…

title: 正統七年會試錄
text:
行立光明正大之事業使人仰其
聲光敬慕其為人以匹休於古之
大賢君子則庶幾不負於科目取
士之盛也衷叨典較文亦與有榮
焉庸敢以是為勉
翰林院侍讀學士奉直大夫苗衷
謹序
alt_text:
行立光明正大之事業使人仰其
聲光欽慕其爲人以匹休於古之
大賢君子則庶幾不負於科目取
士之盛也東叨典較文亦與有榮
焉庸敢以是爲勉
翰林院侍讀學士奉直大夫苗東
謹序
punctuated:
行，立光明正大之事業，使人仰其聲光，敬慕其為人，以匹休於古之大賢君子，則庶幾不負於科目取士之盛也。衷叨典較文，亦與有榮焉，庸敢以是為勉。
翰林院侍讀學士奉直大夫苗衷謹序。
translation_en:
…conduct, and establish illustrious, upright achievements, so that people will look up to their renown and luster and revere and admire their character, matching the glory of the great worthies and superior men of antiquity. Only thus may they perhaps not fail the grand institution of selecting scholars through the examination system. Having had the undeserved honor of presiding over the evaluation of the essays, I, Zhong, also share in the glory; therefore I venture to offer these words as encouragement.
Respectfully prefaced by Miao Zhong 苗衷, Academician Reader-in-Waiting of the Hanlin Academy and Grand Master for훈 [Fengzhi dafu, Grand Master for Comprehensive Duty].
